ai.en: Romeo and Juliet by Ballet Ireland at the Gaiety Theatre, Shakespeare's tale in dance.

events.description: Based on Shakespeare’s tale of star-crossed lovers, Romeo & Juliet is one of the greatest love stories of all time. Against a backdrop of ancient feuds and gang warfare, the ill-fated young couple fall hopelessly in love, but their families are bitter enemies. In order to be together, the two lovers must be prepared to risk everything. Set to Prokofiev’s incredible score, this stunning production blends exquisite choreography by Morgann Runacre-Temple. How far would you go for love… when everything is at stake? A timeless tale. A powerful score. An unforgettable experience. Proudly sponsored by EY, with support from RTÉ Supporting the Arts. events.description: Experience the wonder of Christmas at Elf Town, where families can embark on a magical journey filled with festive fun, enchanting characters and unforgettable memories. The Immersive Experience (75 min): Journey through the enchanting worlds of Elf Town in a fully interactive adventure. Meet magical characters, enjoy festive surprises and experience the wonder of Elf Town before a private visit with Santa. The Magical Santa Visit (30 min): Perfect for families looking for a shorter, more flexible experience. Enjoy some of Elf Town's magical highlights, a special moment with Santa and the excitement of becoming an Honourary Elf. Whichever experience you choose, Elf Town Dublin promises a memorable Christmas adventure for the whole family. title.en: REWORKED: A Zero-Waste Jewellery Workshop with Shock of Grey

ai.en: A zero-waste jewellery workshop with Shock of Grey at IMMA, making jewellery from vintage finds and old beads.

events.description: Create one-of-a-kind jewellery from vintage finds, preloved beads and forgotten treasures in this colourful workshop with Shock of Grey. Explore a collection of reclaimed beads, broken jewellery, chains, charms and other materials, then mix, match and reimagine them to create something completely your own. Learn simple techniques for taking jewellery apart, combining unexpected materials and transforming unwanted pieces into something new and wearable. Bring along old or broken jewellery from home or choose from the materials provided. Suitable for ages 12+, this relaxed workshop offers a playful introduction to creative reuse and zero-waste design. No experience is required and all tools and materials are supplied.

events.description: —until he’s left at the altar and his world is turned upside down. When he meets the charming Julia, sparks fly, but true love proves anything but simple. title.en: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU

ai.en: Common Ground: Ireland in the EU, an EPIC exhibition on Ireland's joining of the European Economic Community in 1973.

events.description: Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size. Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.

ai.en: Gulliver's Travels and Vivaldi's Four Seasons at St Patrick's Cathedral, a Jonathan Swift Festival concert opening with Handel's Messiah overture.

events.description: Opening the programme is the overture from Messiah, first performed in Dublin in 1742. Handel had intended it for St Patrick’s Cathedral, but permission was refused by its then Dean, a certain Jonathan Swift, and the premiere instead took place in the Music Hall on Fishamble Street. Georg Philipp Telemann’s Gulliver Suite, written shortly after the publication of Swift’s novel, transforms its fantastical worlds into musical form. The evening culminates in Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons, here presented with texts by Jonathan Swift. Ticket prices vary. events.description: AGMP presents THE STYLE COUNCILLORS'Our Favourite Shop' 40th Anniversary Tour The Style Councillors are the world’s one and only tribute to The Style Council. 'Our Favourite Shop' is the second studio album by The Style Council released in 1985. The Style Councillors will be celebrating this classic LP by performing selections from the album aswell as the hits and fan favourites of The Style Council. Formed in 2013 by Darren Fletcher (Paul Weller) and Steve Hayes (Mick Talbot), The Style Councillors have quickly built a loyal fanbase for the group which was Paul Weller’s home for the majority of the 1980’s and where he wrote some of his finest songs. Dani Clay (Dee C. Lee) and Craig Read (Steve White) are joined by the Bad Manners Horn Section and a stellar line up of musicians hell-bent on recreating the sound of The Style Council. After the dissolution of The Jam in 1982, Paul Weller joined forces with Mick Talbot, formerly of The Merton Parkas, Dexys Midnight Runners and The Bureau, to form The Style Council. The band released a string of succesful singles between 1983-1989 such as Speak Like a Child, Money-Go-Round, Long Hot Summer, My Ever Changing Moods, You’re The Best Thing, Shout To The Top, Walls Come Tumbling Down, A Solid Bond In Your Heart, Come To Milton Keynes, The Lodgers, Why I Went Missing, and more. events.description: This is a rare opportunity to explore the rich heritage of the Docklands area and uncover the unique story behind the building, its architecture, and its role in shaping the city. The CHQ Building, originally known as Stack A, was constructed in the early 19th century as part of the broader Custom House docks complex. This tour offers the chance to step back in time and discover the building’s original purpose as a bonded warehouse for storing valuable cargo including tobacco, tea, wine and spirits. On the CHQ tour, you’ll also hear the fascinating story of its transformation into a grand Banqueting Hall in 1856, when thousands gathered for an enormous celebration in honour of Irish soldiers returning from the Crimean War.

ai.en: The Pride Tour at EPIC, a look at queer Irish history and global impact, with homosexuality decriminalised in 1993.

events.description: LGBTQ+ equality in Ireland only came relatively recently. Homosexuality was only decriminalised in 1993, with marriage equality following in 2015. However, LGBTQ+ people have always been part of Ireland’s story, and for many, emigration offered the chance to live more openly. Our Pride Tour explores some of these stories, looking at the lives of LGBTQ+ Irish emigrants, activists, artists and other figures who challenged attitudes at home and made their mark around the world. Based in Dublin's Docklands, EPIC tells the true story of the Irish, and acts as the base for the Irish Family History Centre. It also sits across from the Jeanie Johnston Famine Ship, just 2 minutes away.

ai.en: Ardal O'Hanlon's Not Himself at Fitzpatrick Castle Hotel in Killiney on 31 January 2027, part of the Dalkey Comedy Festival.

events.description: Ardal O'Hanlon Live at Fitzpatrick Castle Hotel, Killiney on Jan, 31st 2027 - Part of Dalkey Comedy Festival. Ardal O Hanlon - Not Himself: Oh, it’s all there! All the trademarks are in evidence in Ardal’s latest show. Beautifully crafted stand-up comedy? Yes. Celebrated use of language? Tick. Lateral thinking, surreal flourishes, sharp observations? Of course. As for the occasional profundity? Maybe. Despite his best attempts over many decades to put the world to rights, it is still a colossal mess. And so, Ardal has no choice but to go out on the road again. Like the good comedy doctor he is, he fearlessly diagnoses the various pathologies and neuroses that are currently ravaging humanity. events.description: Even through centuries of war, hardship and poverty, Dublin has always found room for love stories that capture the public imagination. ai.en: Frederick Douglass and his Irish connections at the Ambassador Theatre, about the abolitionist and orator.

events.description: Frederick Douglass (1818–1895) was a renowned African American abolitionist, orator, publisher and author—reportedly the most photographed American of the 19th century. Recently escaped from slavery, Douglass arrived in Dublin in 1845, staying four months to publish his first autobiography, deliver lectures, and meet activists like Daniel O'Connell. He later made four visits to Belfast in 1846. We'll explore Dublin sites tied to his time here, set against political change: relief for Irish Catholics, yet widespread poverty and a famine gripping the countryside. Douglass was deeply moved by Ireland's underclass and those working to relieve it. Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

Tom Dunne (lead singer of Something Happens) and Fiachna Ó Braonáin (founding member of Hothouse Flowers) have joined forces with Alan Connor (pianist with The Late Late Show House Band and long-time member of the Sharon Shannon Band) to form a unique trio: An Evening with Fiachna Ó Braonáin, Tom Dunne and Alan Connor – Songs and Stories This special night features songs from both The Hothouse Flowers and Something Happens and a selection of the trio’s all-time favourite tracks. Between them, Tom and Fiachna have released 11 studio albums (4 of which reached Number One), 7 live albums and undertook an estimated 20 to 25 tours of the US. Alan Connor brings a touch of Billy Preston-style magic to the stage, having played on more albums than one could count. While Tom and Fiachna have crossed paths on the world's stages over the years, the idea of collaborating musically only recently came to life. As Tom puts it: “They seemed like such different worlds. Hothouse Flowers had strong trad and folk influences. Something Happens were so guitar heavy and American-facing, American-produced – hence all those US tours.” Fast forward to now – the trio has played around 50 shows together, and each one has been magical.
